rules.action: Soft-tipped workhorse wire (e.g. Sion Blue, BMW, Fielder FC). Shape a gentle primary curve for most anatomy.

Standard workhorse for crossing; exchange to extra-support wire (e.g. Grand Slam, Iron Man) before device delivery through heavily calcified segments. If balloon won't cross, exchange to Rotawire for atherectomy.
Soft steerable workhorse wire; gentle primary curve only. Avoid over-shaping which straightens the vessel. Microcatheter should be available for wire exchange and distal medication delivery.
Soft steerable workhorse wire; avoid over-shaping the tip. A gentle curve navigates the angle more reliably than an aggressive tip. Microcatheter assists navigation through severe angulation.
Soft-tipped workhorse for crossing; extra-support wire for device delivery after lesion preparation. Consider GEC before escalating wire stiffness.
rules.caution: Avoid aggressive wire manipulation in tortuous segments — perforation risk is elevated.

rules.action: Hydrophilic floppy wire preferred for graft wiring to mitigate plication. Avoid stiff or aggressive wires that risk dissection in degenerated conduits.
Remove SB jailing wire before rotational or orbital atherectomy of the MV — burr entanglement with jailed wire risks catastrophic complications. Re-wire SB after atherectomy.
rules.caution: SB wire entanglement with RA/OA burr can cause wire fracture or vessel perforation.
